messages:
maria_support: FYI ACME (tenant: acme-corp) reported a big tail latency regression after the 03:12 deploy. p95 went from ~120ms to ~900ms, p99 ~2.8s. They see intermittent 504s and a couple of GPU OOMs.
maria_support: Happened on dedicated pool gpu-dedicated-a in us-west2. Customer says traffic pattern hasn't changed.
leo_oncall_runtime: Got it — thanks. Can you paste the earliest OOM log and the worker IDs? Also: are they pinned to a specific model variant?
maria_support: Logs attached (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-16T03:14:09Z] worker-17 runtime ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-16T03:14:09Z] worker-17 runtime WARN: kv_cache_size_mb=18300 slab_usage=0.94
[2026-03-16T03:14:09Z] worker-17 runtime ERROR: token_gen_latency p99=2800ms
```
maria_support: They are on redwood-7b pinned -> redwood-7b:v9
ben_sre: Looks like KV cache growth + high slab occupancy. Can you run the KV heat query in metrics? e.g.
```
-- run in metrics UI
sum(kv_cache_bytes) by (tenant) [5m]
```
ben_sre: If acme-corp shows steady growth near node capacity it's fragmentation + allocator pressure.
leo_oncall_runtime: Quick checks:
- list active KV shards on pool: `adminctl kv list --pool gpu-dedicated-a --tenant acme-corp`
- slab occupancy: `curl -s http://worker-17:9100/metrics | grep slab_occupancy`
nina_custsuccess: I talked to the customer — they can tolerate brief degraded throughput if we route them to a smaller variant. They want a fast mitigation.
alice_runtime_lead: Mitigation plan (short-term):
1) activate tenant-level fallback to compact variant (reduces memory by ~50%)
2) temporarily lower per-tenant max_kv_cache to 8GB
3) if needed, soft-restart the worker process on affected nodes to free fragmented slabs
Commands:
```
# set fallback routing
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/tenants/acme-corp/routing \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"fallback_variant":"redwood-7b-compact"}'

# reduce kv cache for tenant
adminctl tenant update acme-corp --max-kv-mb 8192

# gentle restart of runtime on node
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/worker-17
```
maria_support: Implementing fallback now.
leo_oncall_runtime: Also try enabling allocator defrag and increasing eviction aggressiveness on the pool as a temporary knob:
```
# cluster flag examples (ops only)
clusterctl set-flag gpu-dedicated-a --slab-thermostat=0.6 --kv-evict-threshold=0.8
```
ben_sre: Note: defrag helps but can cause transient latency spikes during compaction. Prefer fallback variant first.
deploy-bot: Rolling back canary of allocator-v2.1 -> allocator-v2.0 in pool gpu-dedicated-a (canary target: worker-17). Rollback started.
monitoring-bot: Metric alert resolved for worker-17: p99 latency dropped from 2800ms -> 320ms within 90s after rollback and fallback routing (alert: p99_tail_latency_acme-corp).
maria_support: Customer confirms fewer 504s. They're still seeing occasional p99 ~500ms for long generates.
leo_oncall_runtime: For the mid-term (next 24-48h) we should:
- run a controlled defrag sweep on cold nodes (off-peak)
- reduce default per-tenant max_kv to avoid unbounded growth
- add an eviction policy per-model to purge stale prefixes older than X hours
ben_sre: I've created a playbook PR with checks to detect KV runaway: if `kv_cache_mb` grows > 70% of node capacity for 10m, auto-route 10% of traffic to compact variants and raise a P2.
alice_runtime_lead: Action items:
- nina: confirm customer OK with compact routing and extended monitoring (owner)
- leo: run offline defrag on two spare nodes and report effect (owner)
- ben: merge PR for KV runaway auto-route and add alert (owner)
- ops: consider increasing pool capacity if we see more tenants near limit next week
nina_custsuccess: Customer accepted compact routing. We'll monitor. Thanks team :thumbsup:
maria_support: I'll keep the thread open. Closing after 24h no regressions.
